game_moneyline_spread.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): margin = strength gap + HFA/neutral +- QB/availability shocks, with per-team possession counts and points-per-possession from opponent-adjusted efficiency (SP+/FEI/EPA, success rate, trench/havoc), tempo mismatch, turnover luck, special teams; then blowout truncation (starters pulled, clock running, FBS-vs-FCS/cupcake mismatches like the FAU -41.5 rung), key numbers 3/7, rest/travel/bye/letdown, weather, roster churn (portal) in early season, coaching change. FBS OT means no ties. Required inputs: schedule-aware team ratings with preseason prior blended to in-season, QB1 status, injuries/depth, HFA and neutral-site flag, rest, weather, spread margin sd and tail, plus a SEPARATE season-level block for the Big10/SEC/Big12/ACC '10+ win teams' counts (correlated Poisson-binomial over a shared schedule: intra-conference games force negative dependence) and KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE (maximum total over ~800 D-I games, a tail/extreme-value problem, not a moneyline). Hazards from rules: KXNCAAFSPREAD text is silent on overtime, WINMARGIN explicitly 'including overtime', 48h postponement rule, 'not started within 48 hours' -> fair price (cancel), HIGHSCORE counts overtime and any D-I game (FCS included) but not conf-championship/bowl, conference-wins markets are regular-season only. Two of the nine live series are really season-aggregate/extreme-value contracts mis-mapped here. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's s1-s5 (rating prior with posterior SD, QB/availability, site/weather/motivation, matchup variance, blowout truncation and lattice) match my chain and the author adds useful new inputs (qb_replacement_value, rating_posterior_sd, mismatch_cover_curve). Differences: (1) the author concedes in s6 and unresolved conf_wins_mechanism that 5 of the 9 live series are season aggregates but defines no inputs/data for them; I require a schedule graph, conference-game dependence and extreme-value inputs; (2) author leaves pace/drives unattached while labelling pace_volume COVERED; (3) author keeps market-derived cfb.score_resid as KEEP_SECONDARY; (4) author asserts SPREAD includes overtime although the SPREAD text is silent (WINMARGIN says it explicitly).

game_stat_props.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): the only live series is KXNCAAFTEAMRECYDS, a TEAM receiving-yards ladder (not a player prop). Chain: offensive plays x pass rate (game script, tempo, weather) -> pass attempts minus sacks/scrambles -> completion rate x air yards x YAC (QB quality, WR corps availability, opponent pass defense/coverage, pressure) -> receiving yards by completions; heavy right tail from explosive plays; garbage-time inflation of passing by trailing teams; QB/WR availability scenario mixture; wind/rain; run-heavy option teams produce near-zero tails. Settlement: yards from completions only (sacks do not subtract from receiving, unlike rushing), 2-pt conversions excluded, first/second overtime counts, postponement 48h. Required inputs: team pass attempts forecast, completion/yards per attempt split, receiver availability, QB identity, opponent pass-defense efficiency, pace, spread/total-implied script (as context only), weather. The archetype definition ('player prop... first downs, TDs') does not match the single live series; no individual-player prop series is live so any player-level inputs would be unconsumed. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (snap budget, script-driven pass share, yards per completion, receiver availability, dispersion, settlement) matches mine, including the correct point that sacks do not reduce receiving yards and that 2-pt yards are excluded. Differences: the author's input set has no QB identity/status input (qb_status_pit lives only in other archetypes) and no non-market rating/expected-margin input, yet script_adjusted_pass_attempts is measured from 'expected margin from non-market ratings'; the BENCHMARK_ONLY team_total_split is still wired into s2; several inputs the author itself marks WEAK (player_usage, injuries, turnover_luck) remain in stages and an interaction.

game_total.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): total = possessions (both teams' tempo, plays/game, run-pass mix, clock rules, no-huddle, turnovers/short fields) x points per possession (opponent-adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency, explosiveness, finishing drives / red-zone TD vs FG, special teams) + overtime points, with blowout truncation (clock-killing run game and backups cut possessions), weather (wind>15mph, rain, cold), QB and OL/skill availability, kicker quality, discrete scoring lumps (3/6/7/8) making key numbers. Ladder rungs are nested events (monotone). KXNCAAFTOTAL sampled rung 25.5 is deep left tail (Nebraska-Illinois), so low-total regime (defensive/ground teams, bad weather) matters for thresholds far from the median. Settlement: rules text says only 'teams collectively score more than X points'; overtime is NOT mentioned in the sampled text (contrast WINMARGIN/1HFT which say 'including overtime') so OT inclusion is unverified; 48h postponement, fair price if not started in 48h. Required inputs: pace, drives, efficiency both sides, explosiveness, red-zone/finishing, turnover/field position, special teams/kicker, weather, QB availability, mismatch/blowout script, OT probability, officiating/penalties. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (possessions x points per possession, scoring-trip efficiency, non-offensive scores, wind exposure, blowout regime, lumpy lattice) matches mine and is stronger on kicker/wind. The author correctly refuses to assume overtime inclusion (text silent). Differences: no overtime inputs are defined under either reading of the contract (tie curve and OT scoring live only in the overtime archetype with no cross-reference); rules_verification says VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT although the single most important settlement fact (OT) is unverified; BENCHMARK_ONLY cfb.score_resid is wired into s4 and the distribution_variance category.

findings.text: No overtime input is defined under either reading of the contract. The record rightly says KXNCAAFTOTAL text is silent on OT, but if OT counts the total needs P(tie after regulation) and OT scoring (cfb.regulation_tie_curve, cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate exist only in the overtime archetype) and if it does not the series is regulation-only; nothing cross-references the overtime archetype or states the conditional input set. Resolution of total_ot_treatment should trigger an explicit input addition.

Weak as an interaction.

This is acknowledged for Open-Meteo vintage fidelity but not for the proxy itself.

overtime.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): KXNCAAFOT = P(regulation ends tied). Distribution of final regulation margin near zero: depends on spread (close games), total (low totals concentrate on ties in a discrete 3/7 scoring space; ties after regulation ~5-8% of FBS games), end-of-regulation clock strategy (kneel to OT vs go for win, FG-on-final-play, timeouts), kicker reliability, coaching aggressiveness. KXNCAAFMOSTOT = season maximum number of OT periods across all D-I games (~800 FBS+FCS games): need P(game reaches OT) x P(continue after OT1, OT2 (possession-based ~25-35% continue each)) x P(continue each 2-pt alternating round from OT3, ~ p^2+(1-p)^2 about 0.5 with 2-pt conversion rate ~45-50%) and then order statistics over N games for a 9+ rung; tail ~0.5^6 given >=3OT. Settlement hazards: an OT counts once it commences via a legal snap (OT1-2) or first 2-pt attempt (3+), partial OT counts in full, scheduled-but-unstarted OT does not count, 'D-I game' includes FCS and the MOSTOT text restricts to the regular season (text truncated in sample; conf-championship/bowl status unverified), 48h postponement. Required inputs: P(tie at end of regulation) from margin distribution, spread/total, kicker, coach/late-game strategy, OT format rule (NCAA 2-pt from 3rd OT), 2-pt conversion rate, number of D-I games remaining (count of games, not just FBS), weather/possession dynamics, historical OT-length distribution. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (tie mass of regulation margin on a 3/7 lattice, end-of-regulation decisions, OT1-2 possession renewal, 2-pt regime from OT3 at about 0.5 per period, season union over N games) matches mine almost point for point and the 0.5^6 tail logic is right. Differences are second order: tie curve is fitted on FBS only while MOSTOT counts all D-I (FBS+FCS) games; BENCHMARK_ONLY market_ratings/team_total_split and WEAK score_resid/blowout_management remain wired into s1/s2 and category coverage; availability_news declared NOT_APPLICABLE although a QB change shifts both mean and SD of the margin.

findings.text: BENCHMARK_ONLY inputs remain wired into the mechanism: cfb.market_ratings is credited as covering talent_strength and is in stage s1; cfb.team_total_split (BENCHMARK_ONLY) is in s1; cfb.score_resid (WEAK) and cfb.blowout_management (WEAK) are in s1/s2 and in category coverage; required_data 'Pre-game ratings' lists market_ratings and team_total_split as fed inputs. The tie curve is explicitly non-market, so these should be dropped from wiring.

Population mismatch: cfb.regulation_tie_curve is fitted on 'all FBS games since 2005 (about 9,000)' while cfb.season_ot_exposure counts FBS plus FCS games (the contract says Division I, text for MOSTOT: 'any Division I game'). FCS tie/OT behaviour (different scoring, kickers, FBS-vs-FCS mismatches) is not modelled and no FCS line-score source is confirmed. Also 2005-2025 is about 21 seasons x roughly 750 FBS games, i.e. about 15,000 games, so the stated 'about 9,000' sample size looks wrong (or the window is not what it says).

availability_news and situational_schedule_motivation are marked NOT_APPLICABLE with the argument that effects only shift the margin mean; a QB change or a late scratch also changes the margin SD and the total, which are the two inputs of the tie curve, so at least a pointer (qb_status_pit via expected margin/total) is needed. The reasons given are long but arguable.

Contract scope: the MOSTOT primary text ('in the 2026 college football regular season') already scopes it to the regular season, and the sibling HIGHSCORE text states conference championship/bowl/CFP games are 'not part of the regular season'. Unresolved 'mostot_scope' and variants say conference-championship status is 'unconfirmed'; it is reasonably established though the sample is truncated at 'regardless of its durat'. Wording overcautious, not blocking.

quarter_and_half_sides.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): period margin = possessions in that period (first-half kickoff/deferral choice decides who gets the ball first and last-before-half, sudden-death possession parity, 2-minute drills) x points per possession in that period; opening-script quality, halftime adjustments, Q4 garbage-time and clock-killing; scoring in single quarters is highly discrete and tie-heavy (0-0, 7-7 quarters are common, so tie probability must be modelled explicitly and the market tie rule matters). Variants: quarter/half winner, period spread (key number 7.5 is nearly a full TD), BTTS in a quarter, highest-scoring-quarter (ties split $1/N rounded down), 1H-tie/game-winner combo (joint distribution of half result and final result including OT). Rules facts: 1H counts only 1st-half points, 2H and 2H spread INCLUDE overtime, 4Q EXCLUDES overtime, QHIGHSCORE excludes OT from Q4. KXNCAAFQF is a season-level 'qualify for CFP quarterfinals' future (mis-mapped here). Tie handling for quarter/half WINNER markets is not visible in the sampled text (truncated at ~900 chars) so is unverified. Required inputs: team-ratings and scoring-rate by period, receive/defer choice and coin toss, opening-drive script (tempo, scripted plays), QB/skill availability, halftime adjustment tendencies, Q4 blowout regime, per-period tie-aware distributions, weather. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (possession order/deferral, per-period scoring, game-margin prior, script, lattice and settlement scope) matches mine and correctly flags that tie payout for period winners is unverified and that KXNCAAFQF is misfiled. Differences: I require a quarter-TOTAL joint model for KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE (pro-rata ties across four quarters) and for the BTTS series, which the margin-only lattice does not give and which lives in the totals archetype without cross-reference; BENCHMARK_ONLY market_ratings/score_resid and the DUPLICATE half_split remain wired into stages; QB status is only secondary.

findings.text: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE (highest-scoring quarter, pro-rata $1/N ties, Q4 excludes OT) and the BTTS series (1Q/2Q/3Q) are in this archetype but need the distribution of each quarter's combined and per-team points jointly across the four quarters, not period margins. The inputs are a margin lattice (period_margin_lattice), q_scoring and corr; the period-total pmf, per-quarter zero-scoring mass and quarter-to-quarter total correlation (cfb.period_total_dispersion, cfb.period_share_of_total) are defined only in the quarter_and_half_totals record with no cross-reference, and nothing models 'argmax over four quarters with tie-splitting'. Required inputs for two live series are missing here.

Present as hypotheses; a KEEP_CONTEXT input cannot anchor a regime-switch claim.

quarter_and_half_totals.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): period total = expected possessions in the period x points per possession in the period + end-of-half effects. Q1 total is low (opening scripts, first drive conservative; many 0-0/7-0 quarters), Q2 includes two-minute drill and end-of-half FG attempts, Q3 is post-halftime (who received kickoff by deferral), Q4 is skewed by blowout/garbage time and trailing-team passing (higher tempo) vs leading-team clock burn; 2H adds OT. Rung 6.5/7.5 are single-TD thresholds so P(total>=8) is a lumpy discrete problem (7+3, 7+7...). 1H TEAM total (KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL) needs team-side share. Rules: 1H counts only 1st-half points; 2H total INCLUDES OT; 4Q total EXCLUDES OT; 1Q/2Q/3Q tickers say only points in that quarter; postponement 48h/fair price. Required inputs: per-period scoring rates, pace by period, deferral/receive, opening script, halftime adjustment, game script, weather, QB availability, per-team first-half scoring share, blowout state. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (game total allocated to periods, drive budget in the period, lumpy points per scoring chance, late script, settlement scope) matches mine and the per-period dispersion and drive-budget inputs are good. Differences: the 2H total includes overtime (verified in KXNCAAF2HTOTAL text, sampled rung 6.5) yet no stage or input models the OT increment or the regulation-tie link (the sides archetype has second_half_ot_spillover, totals has nothing); BENCHMARK_ONLY m.ladder_structure is credited with covering settlement_contract; DUPLICATE half_split and WEAK opening_poss remain wired in; the unresolved claim that the 1H team total text does not state its period is contradicted by the primary text.

findings.text: KXNCAAF2HTOTAL ('2nd half (including overtime)', sampled rung 6.5) is a verified OT-inclusive contract, but no stage, input or interaction in this record models the overtime increment: no P(tie after regulation), no OT points distribution, no second_half_ot_spillover (that input exists only in the sides record). With P(OT)~5-7% and about 7-10 OT points the 2H mean shifts roughly half a point, which moves a 6.5 rung materially. Required inputs missing.

The 1H team-total series has no non-market team-side allocation input (period_share_of_total is game-level).

Contradiction with the text: unresolved 'team_total_period_rules' and the variants say the 1HTEAMTOTAL text does not state that only first-half points count / 'the title defines it'. The primary rules text is explicit: 'If Notre Dame scores over 6.5 points in the 1st half of the Miami (FL) vs Notre Dame ... game'. No left-tail validation is specified.

season_futures.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): season simulation. Game-level win probabilities across the full schedule (ratings, schedule difficulty, HFA, injury risk to QB, in-season rating drift/regression), conference standings tiebreakers (head-to-head, division/no-division formats, top-2 for championship games in SEC/Big12/Big Ten rules), conference title game win prob, then the CFP selection process (committee subjective ranking, strength-of-record, conference champion auto bids/format for 2026, seeding, bye rules, first-round hosting) and bracket progression (QF/SF/final). Season-level contracts in the family: win totals (ties not counted as wins), undefeated regular season, undefeated at home (neutral excluded), H2H wins with tie-market, regular-season top finishers (ties all count as achieved), bowl selection ('selected regardless of competing', FCS playoffs excluded), conference championship qualifier/winner, CFP qualifiers/QF/SF/finalist/seed/top seed, NCAAF title, multi-year 'before 2030' TFUT (needs multi-season roster/coaching/program trajectory model). Required inputs: preseason ratings + roster talent (portal-adjusted), remaining schedule, standings/tiebreaker state, committee behaviour history, injuries/QB, realignment (Pac-12 revival markets), and dated information flow. Dependency across teams is essential (a Poisson-binomial with shared games; conference champions are mutually exclusive). || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (correlated rating draws, QB shocks, schedule path, tiebreakers/title game, committee selection and bracket, multi-year trajectory) matches mine, with good new inputs (remaining_game_win_probabilities, rating_posterior_draws, conference_membership_and_schedule_map). Differences: no stage or input for bowl selection (KXNCAAFBOWLGAME is a live RULES_TEXT series: 6-win eligibility, slots vs eligible teams, conference tie-ins, selection order), none for FCS/Ivy/other non-FBS champion series that are in the ledger, and the settlement summary generalises 'conference champion = wins the title game' beyond the one SEC text actually read.

findings.text: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME ('selected to play in a bowl game or the CFP', RULES_TEXT, selection not participation, eligible-bowl list in the text) has no mechanism, stage or input. Bowl selection depends on 6-win eligibility (and 5-7 teams used when slots exceed eligible teams), number of bowl slots vs eligible teams per conference, conference tie-in and pecking order, bowl committee choices, and CFP/NY6 taking top teams. The record mentions the series only in settlement text; stages s3-s5 cover wins, conference title and committee but not bowl selection. A live rules-text series is unmodelled.

Non-FBS and non-title-game series are in the ledger (KXNCAAFCS and KXNCAAFFCS 'FCS champion', KXNCAAFIVY 'Ivy League Champion', Pac-10, plus MAC/AAC/CUSA/Sun Belt qualifiers) but the mechanism (FCS 24-team playoff bracket and FCS ratings; Ivy has no title game and shared titles; Group-of-Five title-game formats) is not represented. The settlement_definition states 'conference champion markets settle on winning the conference championship game and qualifier markets on being in it', which is read only from the SEC text (KXNCAAFSEC: 'wins the 2026 College Football SEC Championship Game'); for Ivy this is false by construction and for the others it is unread (TITLE_ONLY). Unresolved 'title_only_series' covers the missing text but not the missing FCS/Ivy inputs and data.

Wiring/audit disagreement: BENCHMARK_ONLY cfb.market_ratings and cfb.futures_coherence appear in stages s1/s6; WEAK cfb.season_sim_distribution (an output, not an input) is credited in distribution_variance coverage; cfb.polls (generic) is a retained input; required_data lists no price-free feed that replaces market_ratings for the team prior beyond SP+/own ratings.

coaching_scheme is declared GAP (coach effect not separated from ratings) although the same ledger carries a coach-out hazard archetype whose inputs (coach_exit_hazard_features, buyout exposure) feed directly into multi-year contracts like KXNCAAFTFUT ('before 2030'); no cross-reference. Likewise bracket-stage inputs and the CFP resume model are re-derived here and in the polls archetype separately (duplication risk).

Several quotes establish less than claimed: the KXNCAAFTFUT quote ('after Issuance and before the 2030-31 college football season') shows a multi-year window, but the 'Issuance'-date dependence (eligible only for qualification events after market issuance) and the CFP format uncertainty across 2026-2029 (12 vs 24 teams) make the horizon model much harder than 'AR(1) with shock SD 4'; the parameters 0.7 and 4 are asserted (flagged 'to be fitted') with no source.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: CFBD 'rankings' endpoint for CFP committee history 2014+, ESPN Strength of Record scrape and CFBD portal/returning-production endpoints are treated as available; only portal coverage is flagged. NIL/revenue-sharing data is correctly flagged unavailable.

team_total.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): team points = team possessions x points per possession; team-specific offense vs opponent defense, tempo of both sides, red-zone/finishing, QB/skill availability, game script share of total (favorite's late scoring dampened by blowout management; underdog trailing passes more), special teams/defensive TD contributions, weather, OT points. The KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL rung sampled (New Mexico 45.5) is far right tail of a tempo-heavy offense. Rules text sampled is silent on overtime (same issue as game_total). KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT (team rushing attempts) is NOT a points contract: attempts = plays x run rate x game script (leading teams run more, trailing teams pass), which belongs to a team stat-count archetype. Required inputs: team-side expected points from rating + opponent adjustments, spread/total share (context only), pace, run/pass mix, QB availability, red-zone tendencies, defensive/special-teams scoring rate, weather, rushing attempt model (plays, run rate, lead-time). || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (own drive share, points per drive vs opponent unit, script cap/lift, covariance with opponent score) matches mine and adds good inputs (own_drive_share, leader_scoring_persistence, team_pair_score_covariance). Differences: the author knowingly omits cfb.run_defense (opponent matchup is pass-only) and states so in unresolved; BENCHMARK_ONLY team_total_split and m.ladder_structure and WEAK score_resid are still credited as covering categories; the rush-attempt count series is a stat count filed under a points archetype without a misfile flag; OT inclusion unverified (honestly disclosed).

findings.text: The matchup input set is knowingly one-sided: cfb.run_defense is in the catalog but not attached, so a run-first offence meets only overall def_ppa (unresolved 'run_defense_matchup_gap' and the secondary_coverage audit both say this). The author's own interaction 2 (style x opposing unit quality) cannot be tested with only the pass half of the opposing defence. The required input list is incomplete by admission; attach run_defense (and an opponent rush-yards-allowed measure) rather than deferring.

Wiring/audit disagreement: BENCHMARK_ONLY cfb.team_total_split is in s3 and credited as covering game_context_script; BENCHMARK_ONLY m.ladder_structure is in s5 and credited as covering settlement_contract; WEAK cfb.score_resid is in s4 and distribution_variance coverage.

KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT (team rushing attempts, TITLE_ONLY) is a stat-count contract, not a points total; the record bolts it onto this archetype via script_rush_attempts and a settlement paragraph but does not flag it as misfiled (compare the record for quarter_and_half_sides, which does flag KXNCAAFQF). Its mechanism (plays x run share, sacks counted as rush attempts under NCAA stats) belongs with the stat-count archetypes and the 'sacks count as rushes' point is unverified for the contract.

Settlement: record is honest that overtime is unstated in KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL, but like game_total it defines no OT input (tie curve/OT scoring) and gives no conditional plan; the 'one game in fifteen' OT incidence is asserted. Evidence quote 3 is a market title, not rules text.

The sampled rung (New Mexico over 45.5) is a far-right-tail rung; the dispersion model (team_pair_score_covariance with sign change 'across regimes') is asserted without a stated functional form beyond binned correlations with shrinkage; the claim that own/opponent correlation 'changes sign' is a hypothesis and should be labelled as such.

touchdown_scorer.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): live series are all TEAM or GAME TD counts: first team to score a TD (incl. defensive/special-teams, OT first TD counts, 'no team scores TD' outcome), total TDs both teams, team rushing TDs, team receiving TDs, team total TDs, defence/special-teams TD (1+ across both teams, first two OT count). Chain: team TD count = drives x TD-per-drive (red-zone finishing, goal-line rushing share, pass vs run TD split by game script) + non-offensive TD (pick-sixes, fumble returns, kick/punt returns/blocks; rare event Poisson ~0.2-0.3/game combined?), minus 2-pt-conversion exclusion; first-TD-team = who gets first possession (coin toss, deferral) x P(TD on drive) with first-score race (hazard model by drive). Hazards: rushing/receiving TDs excluded if scored by another player after fumble recovery; 2-pt conversions do not count in any; OT TDs count. NO player-level 'anytime scorer' series is live, though the archetype definition ('named player scores a touchdown, anytime or first') implies one; nothing in live series needs red-zone carry share by player except as a split of team rushing TDs. Required inputs: drives, TD rate per drive, rush/receive TD split, opening possession, D/ST TD propensity (turnovers forced, return units), weather, QB availability, goal-line usage. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author correctly identifies that all live series are team/game TD counts or a first-team race, and the chain (trips x TD per trip, rush/receive split, first-TD race hazard, D/ST TDs, dispersion) matches mine. Differences: the number of scoring trips/drives (pace) is not an input at all (td_per_scoring_trip is a rate; pace_volume is declared COVERED by it plus the BENCHMARK_ONLY team_total_split), no non-market strength/expected-points, QB status or weather input is attached although the author says these matter; seven inputs the author itself audits WEAK or BENCHMARK_ONLY are still wired into stages s1-s5 and category coverage.

findings.text: The volume side of the touchdown count is not an input. cfb.td_per_scoring_trip is a rate and its measurement says 'Expected team TDs = expected trips x TD per trip', yet no input measures expected trips/drives/plays (cfb.pace, cfb.drives, cfb.expected_possessions are not attached); pace_volume is declared COVERED by ['td_per_scoring_trip','team_total_split'] (the second BENCHMARK_ONLY) and the stage note says 'pace itself is not attached ... the trips input embeds it' (it does not; it is a per-trip rate). Likewise talent_strength is covered by td_per_scoring_trip plus the benchmark, with the text admitting 'team-strength ratings exist ... but are not attached'; QB status ('the main news items (quarterback) are not attached here') and weather ('No weather input is attached') are conceded in the record. A team-TD count model cannot be built from the listed inputs.

Seven inputs the author's audit rates WEAK or BENCHMARK_ONLY are still wired into the mechanism: td_rates, player_usage, depth_chart (s2), dvp (s3), in_game_exit_risk (s4), suspension_eligibility, transfer_roster (s5), team_total_split (s1) and category coverage (role_personnel via depth_chart, opponent_matchup via dvp, availability via suspension_eligibility). The audit says they apply only to a named-player market that does not exist in the live ledger; as wired the record implies inputs are relied on that it has rejected. Meanwhile the archetype key 'touchdown_scorer' maps to zero named-player series (unresolved 'player_series_missing'); it should be re-keyed as team/game TD counts.

KXNCAAFTEAMTD ('Team Total Touchdowns') and KXNCAAFDSTTD/TEAMRECTD/TEAMRSHTD are TITLE_ONLY or partially read; the claim in s1/summary that team total TD counts 'defensive and special-teams touchdowns' is assumed. The settlement for KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD is read correctly (another player's fumble-recovery TD is not rushing), but the record says RECTD/RSHTD texts are truncated after '2-point conversions ... do not count fo' and assumes the rest.

cfb.first_td_race_rate treats the first-TD race as drive-index hazards but ignores that defensive/special-teams TDs can precede any offensive possession ending and that FIRSTTDTEAM has a 'No team scores a TD' outcome settled only 'in the full game (including overtime)'; the model must therefore carry a no-TD mass conditional on regulation scoreless play plus OT. Mentioned in nonlinearities but no input defines the OT touchdown component.

Interaction 4 ('dst_td_propensity x td_per_scoring_trip x td_count_dispersion') is not a genuine interaction: td_count_dispersion is an output distribution parameter, and the stated feedback (a D/ST TD raises the opponent's chance of trailing and passing) is a script effect that would be tested with expected margin, which is not an input here.

unreg:awards_and_honors.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): two contract families. (a) Statistical leaders (most rushing/receiving/passing TDs/sacks in D-I or a conference over the regular season, conference championship excluded, ties pay $1/N, DNP-in-conference resolves No): leader of a max over ~N players: usage/touches share, team pass/run volume, games played (12 vs 13, byes, suspensions), injury hazard, QB/team scheme, schedule difficulty, blowout rest, late-season availability; heavy dependence on number of games and injury survival. (b) Voted awards (Biletnikoff, AP conference POY/DPOY, Bear Bryant coach, finalists; plus NFL-draft declaration): voter narrative, team success, statistical production vs peers, position bias, preseason hype, timing of ballots (AP conference awards after the regular season), finalist-announcement rules (if finalists not announced before winner -> all No), multi-winner ties split $1/N. NFL Draft declaration is a person-decision event (portal/draft-stock/NIL) mis-grouped with awards. Required inputs: player production forecast per category, player availability/injury, team context, award-voting history, voter composition, award-specific criteria, draft-decision signals (draft projections, NIL, eligibility), tie handling. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's two-family split (order-statistic leader races; voted awards/finalists/coach) plus a person-decision (draft) matches mine, including participation/No, 1/N ties and the finalist-not-announced clause. Differences: defensive voted awards (AP DPOY x4 live) have no defensive production feature set beyond a generic percentile; NFL draft declaration is a person decision that the author notes in variants but does not flag as misfiled; WEAK offensive inputs (pass_efficiency, qb_rushing, td_rates) still cover efficiency_conversion/role_personnel although no live series needs them.

findings.text: Defensive voted awards (four live KXNCAAF*AWARD AP DPOY series) and sack/TFL leader series are covered by an offence-centric input set: pass_efficiency, qb_rushing, td_rates (all audited WEAK yet still in s2 and efficiency_conversion/role_personnel coverage) and a generic 'stat percentile' in award_vote_feature_model. No defensive production/usage feature (pass-rush snaps, pressures, havoc, sacks per game) is defined for a DPOY vote model; the record mentions 'pass-rush snaps' only in an audit sentence.

KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE is a player-decision market grouped with awards. variants notes 'Six different mechanisms share this archetype' but unresolved omits a misfile item (compare sides/QF), and the same decision (declare for the NFL Draft is an explicit outcome leg of KXNCAAFTRANSFER in the coaching archetype) is modelled twice (draft_declaration_propensity vs transfer_destination_candidate_model) with no cross-reference; eligibility ('draft-eligible indicator: years since high school >= 3') is stated without a source.

Several statements are asserted, not read: the three-way electorate description (AP writers for conference awards, a foundation panel for Biletnikoff, a coaches/writers panel for coach awards) and 'ballot collected at a fixed date before bowls' have no source in the rules text; status 'inactive' for four AP award tickers in the evidence means ballots/timing may differ from the assumed schedule. Label as MECHANISM_UNCERTAIN or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: leaders are settled on 'recorded' stats; the record notes the official provider is unknown but plans CFBD/NCAA leaderboards. For ties and stat corrections (NCAA leaderboards revise after games; season-end official figures can differ from CFBD sums by tens of yards) no timestamp/vintage rule is specified in required_data beyond 'stat corrections timestamped', and transfers within a season are irrelevant (no mid-season FBS transfer) while conference-membership matters for conference leaders (player 'does not play in the ACC' clause).

Interaction 3 (coach_overperformance_index x standings x award_vote_distribution, 'threshold') and interaction 5 (leader_race_state x schedule_strength x qb, conditional) are plausible but the second's driver (team continues to pass) is not an input; and cfb.leader_race_state mixes current leaderboard, projection and probability-of-overtaking in one 'input' (it is a model output, partly a model).

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): head-coach-out hazard (fired/resign/leave or announced) = f(record vs expectation, rivalry/conference losses, buyout and contract, AD/president/booster pressure, outside poaching incl. NFL, age/retirement, scandal), clustered around the regular season end/Black Friday and Dec 1 etc.; next-head-coach is a categorical choice among candidates (AD search behaviour, assistant promotions, alumni, G5-to-P4 pipeline; interim excluded; no permanent coach by deadline -> all No). Governance: CFP 24-team approval (a decision by commissioners/presidents; 'binding approval AND news confirmation within window'; implementation season irrelevant), conference leave/join (announcements/binding agreements count even if effective later), player transfer destinations (portal windows, NIL, coach change, roster needs; outcome set includes 'stays', 'declares for draft', which settle Yes on separate legs). Required inputs: coach-level hazard factors, contract/buyout data, candidate pools, governance calendar and voting bodies, news-source timing, portal calendar, plus a clear time window. The archetype mixes four unrelated mechanisms (coach exit, coach hire, governance decision, player decision); KXNCAAFTRANSFER is a player decision market inside it. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (exit hazard relative to expectation with buyout and calendar clustering, candidate multinomial with timing failure, vote-count threshold for CFP, feasibility state for realignment, portal destination) matches mine and is among the strongest records. Differences: the inputs the author audits IRRELEVANT/WEAK (suspension_eligibility, opt_out_departures, roster_continuity) are still listed in stage s3; m.lifecycle/m.rules_text are referenced in stages but not audited; playoff_format (a format table) is credited as the governance rules layer; the player-decision market (TRANSFER, with 'declare for draft' as an outcome) duplicates the draft-declaration model in the awards archetype without cross-reference.

findings.text: Audit/wiring disagreement: cfb.suspension_eligibility (IRRELEVANT), cfb.opt_out_departures (WEAK) and cfb.roster_continuity (WEAK) are still input_ids of stage s3; m.lifecycle and m.rules_text are used in stage/coverage but are not in input_audit or new_inputs; cfb.playoff_format (audited KEEP_CONTEXT, 'a format table') is credited as the governance rules layer in officiating_rules coverage though CFP expansion is a vote, not a format table.

KXNCAAFTRANSFER (Arch Manning, outcomes: stays at Texas, declares for the draft, commits to another school) is a player decision with a multi-outcome settlement whose 'declare for the draft' leg duplicates KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE (awards archetype) and 'stay' leg interacts with transfer-portal withdrawal rules; the record models a single transfer_destination_candidate_model as secondary/player_role. The destination decision hinges on NIL/revenue-sharing offers, which the record itself says are unobservable (transfer_compensation_data). Consider re-keying out of this archetype; as listed the model has no usable primary feature.

Contract detail verified correctly but under-used: COACHLEAVE/COACHOUT count an announced departure ('or has announced that they will do so before Dec 1, 2026') and KXNCAAFNEXTCOACH resolves No for all if no permanent coach is announced by Sep 1, 2027; the hazard model must therefore treat 'announced retirement/leave' and 'leaves for another job' (poaching) as qualifying and an interim as non-qualifying. coach_exit_hazard_features lists retirement age but no 'poached by another program/NFL' competing risk.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: USA Today coach salary database covers public-school head coaches' contract summaries, not assistants or most private schools (acknowledged for private schools); the claim that buyout step-downs (Jan 1/Jun 30) can be computed 'from contract terms' requires the contracts themselves via open records (slow, partial) - treat the exposure input's coverage as unknown rather than 'partial yes'.

Small-sample honesty is good (15-25 changes a year), but the proportional-hazard model with a dozen features and rivalry/consecutive-loss effects cannot be validated at that sample; the record does not fix a prior-only fallback (base rate by calendar window) as the default when the covariate model is not validated.

unreg:polls_and_cfp_rankings.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): AP voters (62 sportswriters) and the CFP committee (13 members) update a ranking from the prior ranking plus the week's results: inertia/sticky prior, margin and opponent-quality adjustments, loss penalty (losses drop a team more early), bye-week drift, 'quality win' bonus, ranking of teams that did not play. The contract set: AP #1 any week (union over ~17 polls incl Preseason and Final), distinct #1 count (churn; depends on upsets of #1 and parity), final AP #1 (after national title game, expected Jan 26 2027), top-25 at week 5, CFP #25 and top-4 at Nov 24 (CFP committee weeks; if no ranking labelled Nov 24 -> next published). Poll mechanics: AP voters rank all 25; ties impossible but 'week labels'; CFP committee (unlike AP) emphasises strength-of-record/schedule, head-to-head, conference championships, and re-ranks from scratch weekly. Required inputs: current poll ranking and points history, game results and schedule for next 1-3 weeks, team strength rating, resume metrics (SOR/SOS), upset probability of #1, voter behaviour model, CFP committee behaviour, calendar of publication dates. Hazards: poll labelled by AP's official designation (not other sites), CFP schedule shifts. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's chain (results move ballots, inertia and asymmetric loss penalty, succession chain at #1, committee resume ranking, boundary density, release-label mapping) matches mine and the poll_release_calendar input is a good catch. Differences: the Final-AP-#1 series (KXNCAAFAPRANK) is essentially P(national champion), which needs the bowl/CFP bracket simulation from the season-futures archetype; no input or cross-reference supplies that; off_ppa/def_ppa are audited DUPLICATE_OF sp_plus yet remain in s1; WEAK motivation still covers a category.

findings.text: KXNCAAFAPRANK (Final AP Poll #1; rules text: 'Final Rankings (expected to be released on Jan 26, 2027)') depends on bowl and CFP results through the national championship. The record's own evidence note says 'bowl and CFP results are part of the information set', but no stage or input supplies a playoff-bracket/national-title probability (that machinery lives only in season_futures) and the AP-vs-committee champion link (AP voters nearly always rank the CFP champion #1) is absent. The same applies to KXNCAAFAPANY/APCHURN late-season paths. The input list as written cannot price the Final-#1 series.

Wiring/audit disagreement: cfb.off_ppa and cfb.def_ppa are audited DUPLICATE_OF:cfb.sp_plus yet remain in stage s1; WEAK cfb.motivation covers situational_schedule_motivation. cfb.poll_voter_behavior (label retained, audited KEEP_PRIMARY) overlaps cfb.poll_transition_model and cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features; state which supersedes which.

Release mapping detail: for KXNCAAFTOPAPRANK ('Week 5') and CFP 'Nov 24' contracts the record notes AP 'Week 5' is the fifth numbered poll, but the Preseason poll is labelled 'Preseason' and the Week numbering is AP's own label; poll_release_calendar needs the season-by-season AP label table (not just dates) and the CFP release schedule (released on a Tuesday; Nov 24 2026 is a Tuesday) with the stated fallback. The record has this in measurement text but treats the unfilled '|| Time Period ||' defect as a unresolved curiosity; it may recur in other CFP tickers and should be checked against all KXNCAAFCFPPOLL live tickers (it is a settlement-risk item).

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: AP poll points and first-place votes (needed for ballot_points_gap and bubble_proximity_state) exposed by CFBD rankings (flagged) and 'others receiving votes' lists on AP's site; AP Top 25 archive 'since 1990 (free)' unverified, and individual ballots are asserted public but 'not collected in any free structured database' without a check.

Interaction 1 (poll_transition_model x poll_voter_behavior x schedule_strength) lists poll_transition_model, a model output that already contains the stated loss/rank/opponent terms, as an input to its own interaction; the multiplicative claim is testable on the transition model's own coefficients, not as three inputs.

unreg:team_event_counting_specials.rederivation_notes: OWN CHAIN (pre-read): each live series is a count or rare event: team total yards (=rushing + receiving yards, sacks and kneels counting as negative rushing; 2-pt excluded; OT counts), defensive interceptions, sacks, forced turnovers, field goals (team and game total), 2-pt conversion in regulation only, weather delay. Count stats = opportunities x conversion: defensive INT = opponent pass attempts x INT rate (QB quality, pressure, coverage), sacks = opponent dropbacks x sack rate (OL pass-pro vs rush defense, blitz, game script), forced turnovers (INT+fumbles recovered; turnover on downs excluded per rules text), FG made = red-zone stalls x kicker accuracy x distance profile, two-point conversions = attempt probability (TD margin, coach analytics, late-game chart) x success; team yards = plays x yards/play. Weather delay = lightning/severe storm hazard by venue, month, dome, kickoff time; settlement counts delayed starts and suspensions; delays unrelated to weather do not count. Required inputs: plays/drive volume, opponent pass-rush/protection, QB turnover-worthy plays, kicker accuracy and range, coach 2-pt aggressiveness, venue weather/lightning protocol and forecast, and OT adjustments. Hazards: first/second OT counted; 2-pt attempt stats excluded from INT/sack/turnover counts; 2PT market regulation only; delay market excludes non-weather delays. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING THE RECORD: the author's per-series chains (opportunity count x rate per opportunity, decisions that create opportunities, environment, overdispersed small counts, series-specific scope) match mine and are well specialised (dropbacks for sacks/INT, kick attempts and distance for FG, TD-scoring for 2-pt, lightning hazard for delay). Differences: all seven new inputs are labelled primary; the net-yards input claims sacks count as rush ATTEMPTS 'confirmed by the series note' but the note only says negative rushing YARDS; the availability category is left as GAP though kicker/QB/pass-rusher status is plainly required; the dropback-volume and state-dependent-pace constructs duplicate script_adjusted_pass_attempts/state_dependent_pace in the stat-props archetype.

findings.text: cfb.net_yards_per_play_model states sacks are rush attempts 'confirmed by the series note that sacks and kneels are negative rushing yards'. The note (KXNCAAFTEAMYDS: 'total yards ... equals its total rushing yards plus total receiving yards. Sacks and quarterback kneels count as negative rushing yards') confirms yardage accounting only; it says nothing about attempt counting. For total yards the distinction is harmless, but the stated confirmation overreaches (and the same assumption reappears in team_total.script_rush_attempts).

Role inflation: all seven new inputs are labelled primary, including series-specific ones (weather_delay_hazard for one series, two_point_attempt_model for one series). A primary label should denote a driver across the archetype; the existing audit properly demotes pace/drives/etc., then everything new is primary. Re-label.

availability_news is a GAP although the series depend on named-player availability: TEAMSACK/TEAMINT/TEAMTO on QB and pass-rusher status, TEAMFG/TOTALFG on kicker status (cfb.kicker is an input but its availability vintage is only a required_data line 'Pregame personnel vintages' feeding the QB/kicker inputs). The record labels this 'plausible but untested'; the inputs already fed by that dataset cover it, so the category is partly covered and the GAP label is inconsistent.

Cross-archetype duplication: cfb.opp_dropback_volume (this record) and cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts + cfb.state_dependent_pace (stat-props record) measure the same quantity (dropbacks under expected script) under different names with near-identical measurement text; team stat-count series are split across four archetypes (RECYDS: stat props; TEAMYDS/SACK/INT/TO/FG/2PT: specials; TEAMRSHATT: team_total; RSHTD/RECTD/TEAMTD: touchdown) with different input sets. Merge/alias in the catalog. Evidence also types KXNCAAFTEAMYDS as 'rules_review_correction', an unclassified ledger oddity worth checking.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: weather_delay_hazard assumes CFBD or another source has documented delay records back to 2010 (the record says delay history 'reconstructable' from game notes), that NCAA/conference lightning protocol (suspend at threat within 6-8 miles, 30-minute reset) maps onto the contract's 'officially delayed' wording, and that NWS thunderstorm probability and GLM lightning archives are usable at game-window granularity; the record lists these as unverified but still labels the input primary/pregame_knowable partial.
